articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals for Iran-Related Activities
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026. These actions target individuals and entities involved in activities supporting the Iranian regime.

The designations aim to disrupt networks that contribute to Iran's destabilizing actions and its pursuit of illicit programs. Further details on the specific individuals and entities designated were made available on OFAC's website.
This move underscores the U.S. government's ongoing commitment to countering Iran's proliferation activities and its support for terrorism through the use of economic sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Cyber-Related and Transnational Criminal Organization Designations, Targets Cuba
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued new designations on November 5, 2026, targeting cyber-related activities and transnational criminal organizations. Concurrently, OFAC also announced new Cuba-related designations and published a determination related to Cuba.

The Cuba-related determination, pursuant to Executive Order 14404, applies to the electronics, manufacturing, marine, and technology sectors of the Cuban economy, enabling sanctions on foreign persons operating in these areas.
These actions are part of a broader effort to address threats to U.S. national security and foreign policy posed by the Cuban government and to disrupt illicit financial networks.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran Designations, Alert on 'Shadow Fleet,' and Amends Venezuela GL
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and updates to certain Iran-related listings on November 4, 2026.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC published an Iran-related Alert titled 'Iranian Shadow Fleet Reliance on False Flags for Sanctions Evasion,' highlighting the risks associated with providing services to vessels using deceptive practices to circumvent sanctions.

Additionally, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License 5AA, 'Authorizing Certain Transactions Related to the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5 Percent Bond on or After December 18, 2026,' and an amended Frequently Asked Question (FAQ 595).

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Iran-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the issuance of an amended Iran-related General License on October 29, 2026. This amendment modifies existing authorizations concerning transactions related to Iran.
The specific details of the changes within the amended General License were not immediately detailed in the announcement but are available on OFAC's recent actions page.
This action reflects OFAC's ongoing review and adjustment of its sanctions programs to ensure they remain effective and targeted.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals for North Korea and DRC Activities
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in activities related to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).
These designations aim to disrupt illicit networks supporting North Korea's weapons programs and those contributing to instability and human rights abuses in the DRC.
The action underscores the U.S. government's commitment to using sanctions to address global security threats and promote human rights.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Settles with OFAC for Russia Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. on October 27, 2026.
Extreme Networks, a North Carolina-headquartered cloud networking solutions provider, agreed to pay $1,529,685 to settle apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.
The violations involved the export of networking equipment and services to a Russian defense manufacturer that was blocked by operation of law due to its majority ownership by a designated entity.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Reporting
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on October 26, 2026.
These amendments pertain to guidance regarding blocking and rejecting transactions, as well as filing reports with OFAC.
The updates are part of OFAC's ongoing review process to ensure that published guidance remains current and provides clarity for compliance professionals.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran, Russia General Licenses; Removes Belarus, North Korea Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026.
Concurrently, OFAC removed certain Belarus and North Korea designations from its Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List.
Additionally, OFAC issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended several Frequently Asked Questions to provide further guidance.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities Under PAIPA, Issues Associated General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026.

These designations targeted five entities, including Shanghai Zhisuan Technology Co Ltd and Qiji Chuangtan Beijing Investment Management Co Ltd, in connection with the theft of trade secrets from U.S. persons.

OFAC also issued PAIPA General License 1, 'Transactions Authorized Pursuant to the Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations,' and PAIPA General License 2, 'Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving Certain Entities Blocked on October 19, 2026.'

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License and FAQ

This General License, titled 'Authorizing Transactions Related to Earthquake Relief Efforts in Venezuela,' modifies existing authorizations for certain activities in the country.
Additionally, OFAC issued one amended Frequently Asked Question, FAQ 1263, to provide further clarification on the updated license.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Pays $1,529,685 for Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider, has agreed to pay $1,529,685 to settle apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme Networks exported networking equipment and services to a Russian defense manufacturer that was blocked by operation of law due to its majority ownership by a designated entity.

articles.headline: BIS Streamlines Export Controls for Sound Suppressors
body: The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced that as of November 20, 2026, the export of certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors will be subject to BIS's Export Administration Regulations (EAR), rather than the State Department's U.S. Munitions List.

This deregulatory action aims to align export controls on suppressors with those already applied to firearms, reducing the compliance burden on the firearms industry while maintaining national security.

Under this new rule, suppressors will be added to the Commerce Control List (CCL), and a BIS license will be required for certain exports, reexports, or in-country transfers, with applicable license exceptions for firearms also extending to suppressors.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.
